Height calibration

The height is computed from the barometric pressure and a sea-level reference pressure. The options differ in how that reference is found.

  • Standard atmosphere: uses a fixed 1013.25 hPa. No setup needed, but real sea-level pressure varies with the weather, so the absolute height can be off by 250 m or more, and weather changes look like height changes.
  • Manual: you enter your current height and the app calibrates against it. Accurate as long as the weather stays stable; recalibrate when it changes. The field starts with the last calibrated height, or 100 m.
  • GPS altitude: the reference is recalibrated from the GPS altitude (mean-sea-level altitude on Android 14 and later). Needs location permission and a view of the sky; fixes with a poor vertical accuracy are ignored.
  • Weather service: the current sea-level pressure for your location is fetched from open-meteo.com. Needs location permission and an internet connection. Only your approximate coordinates are sent.

If GPS or the service is unavailable, the last reference is kept; before the first one, the standard atmosphere is used.

Calibrate (GPS / weather)

  • At app start: calibration runs once when the app starts and again whenever you change the mode. Use Calibrate now to repeat it at any time; in manual mode it recalibrates to the entered height. The button is disabled for the standard atmosphere and for continuous calibration.
  • Continuous: GPS calibration repeats about every 10 minutes and weather calibration about every 30 minutes while the app is open.

Pressure history

The time span shown by the graph: 30 minutes up to 24 hours. Up to 24 hours of data are stored on the device, but only while the app is open.

Background recording

When switched on, the barometer is recorded every 10 minutes even while the app is in the background or closed (every 10 seconds while the app is open). Recording switches off automatically after 24 hours; switch it on again to continue. A notification is shown while recording, with a Stop button.

Power: this uses a little more battery. The barometer itself uses very little power, and readings are batched so the phone can sleep between them, but the recording service keeps running permanently and some phones may limit it with battery optimisation. Switch it off when you do not need it. Recording does not resume after a reboot.

Compass

The red triangle marks magnetic north, and the bronze triangle marks true north. With Show true north switched on (the default), the degree scale and the heading readout are aligned with true north; the red triangle then shows where magnetic north is. The difference is the magnetic declination for your location. This needs location permission; the last known location is used and no continuous tracking takes place. Without it, or when the option is off, the scale is aligned with magnetic north.

Chart orientation

Pressure up (the default) draws higher pressure towards the top of the chart, so the height scale on the right increases downwards. Height up inverts the chart so that height increases upwards and pressure downwards.

Pressure unit

hPa, atm or mmHg. Applies to the pressure field and the graph.

Height unit

Metric (metres) or imperial (feet). Applies to the height field, the manual height and the graph.

Status line

The bottom of the main screen shows whether the barometer works, the compass accuracy (move the phone in a figure eight if it is low) and the current height calibration.
